why: Click -> ink: the milliseconds between the gesture and the first frame that has PAINTED the answer. One threshold, written once, for the three most frequent gestures. Measured by tests/e2e/ink-latency.spec.ts, judged by scripts/check-ink-latency.ts. Nothing else may hold a copy of these numbers.

budget.rationale: 100ms is the ceiling under which a response to a direct gesture is read as instantaneous rather than as a delay; past it the app stops feeling like a surface being manipulated. It is one number for all three gestures on purpose: a per-gesture budget fitted to today's measurement would have to be re-fitted on every machine, and would turn ordinary scheduling noise into red. The median says 'how long it usually takes'; the max says 'and no single one of them stalled', which is the half a median cannot see - the defect this budget was written after was one sample at 196ms among four at 13ms.

baseline.how: 5 samples per gesture, headless Chromium 1280x800, isolated test server, Apple Silicon. Four consecutive runs.

card.what: click a board card -> its title is readable in the task drawer

tab.what: click another pane tab -> that chat's own message is readable

send.what: press Enter in the composer -> the sent message is readable in the list

firstOpenOfAChat.what: clicking a chat that has never been opened in this session, until its transcript is painted
firstOpenOfAChat.whyNotGatedHere: It is not the same gesture as switching between two open chats, and it is not slow by accident. Probed on 2026-08-14: the message is in the DOM at +39ms and painted at +357ms, with ZERO long tasks and every request answered inside 8ms. Nothing computes during that gap - MessageList.tsx holds the list at `visibility:hidden` behind a skeleton for at least LIST_REVEAL_FLOOR_MS (320ms) so nobody watches react-virtuoso measure heights and re-anchor, a reflow worth a CLS of 0.296 on its own (refresh-cls.spec.ts). The four runs land within 6ms of each other: it is a constant, not noise.
firstOpenOfAChat.howItWouldBeGated: By the constant that causes it, not by a stopwatch: if LIST_REVEAL_FLOOR_MS changes, this number changes with it by construction. Folding it into `tab` would park a permanent 355ms sample inside a 250ms ceiling and hide every real regression behind it - the same mistake this budget already refuses to make for `send`.
